title: Nerja, the pearl of the Costa del Sol
summary: A white village with an Andalusian soul and an international feel, between sea and mountains, with a privileged microclimate and light almost all year round.
body: Nerja is regarded by many as the true pearl of the Costa del Sol: it has kept its Andalusian character while remaining international and welcoming. Unlike more built-up resorts such as Marbella or Torremolinos, there are no high-rises here, just a charming white village, ideal for a relaxed holiday as a couple or with family.

Its great landmark is the Balcón de Europa, a viewpoint on a clifftop with stunning views of the Mediterranean and of the mountains that surround the town, which almost reach 2,000 metres. It is one of those places that take your breath away, especially at sunset.

The natural setting is just as spectacular. The Sierras de Tejeda, Almijara and Alhama Natural Park creates a unique contrast between sea and mountains. In the Maro area, a hamlet belonging to Nerja, you will find the Maro-Cerro Gordo Cliffs, a protected area of great beauty, and the Maro Waterfall, one of the few freshwater falls that flow straight into the Mediterranean.

One of its greatest privileges is the climate: between 300 and 320 days of sunshine a year and very mild winters, with daytime temperatures often above 20°C and rarely below 5°C at night; frosts are practically unheard of. Thanks to the surrounding mountains, Nerja enjoys a genuine microclimate: in summer it usually ranges between 26 and 32°C and only once or twice a season does it top 40°C, unlike Málaga, where the dreaded "terral" (a hot, dry wind) blows in more often.

Nerja also has strong cultural value thanks to the legendary Spanish TV series "Verano Azul", filmed here: Chanquete's famous boat is preserved in the Verano Azul Park. And on the outskirts lie the impressive Caves of Nerja, a cave system of great geological and archaeological value, with some of the most spectacular formations in the world and records recognised in the Guinness Book of Records.

Its location is strategic: Málaga is under an hour away by car and Granada about an hour; Córdoba, Seville and Almería are all reachable within a few hours. And some 90 minutes away is Sierra Nevada, the southernmost ski resort in Europe, so on a single trip you can combine the Mediterranean sea with the snow.

title: Beaches and coves of Nerja
summary: A complete guide: town beaches, hidden coves and the unspoilt beaches of the Natural Park, with parking tips.
body: One of Nerja's greatest riches is its variety of beaches, easy to reach on foot or by car. From our apartments you can walk to several of them in about 12 minutes, or drive there in under five.

Parking in the centre. Balcón de Europa underground car park: paid, three floors, behind the Town Hall with access from Calle La Cruz; handy for the town coves such as Calahonda or El Salón. Los Huertos car park: very large, also paid and open-air; it lets you walk both to the centre and to the Carabeo neighbourhood (including the picturesque Carabeillo) and, via the Mirador del Bendito, down to Burriana beach.

Burriana beach, the most emblematic: a wide range of water sports, full facilities and plenty of restaurants, bars and beach bars. From here you can kayak to the Maro waterfall in about half an hour. It is best not to arrive after 10:00, as the free parking fills up and the beach gets crowded; there is also a paid car park.

La Torrecilla beach, central and very popular: nearby are some of Nerja's main hotels, such as the Riu Mónica and the Perla Marina. At its western end stand the remains of a Nasrid watchtower (13th-15th century) that gives the area its name. Parking is tricky in summer, but with a little patience it is possible.

El Playazo, the favourite of many locals: a long beach stretching west, with plenty of free parking right by the sand, three new beach bars and a boat-hire stand. Ideal if you are after space, quiet and a local feel.

Güilche beach, a secret very close by: to the west, towards Torrox Costa along the old N-347, just six minutes by car. You go down some steps to a cove ringed by rocks, perfect for diving and snorkelling thanks to its underwater formations and marine life; on calm days the water is crystal clear and dolphins are sometimes spotted. Up on the cliff, beside the road, is the El Mirador de Güilche restaurant, highly recommended for its views.

Unspoilt beaches of the Natural Park: within the Maro-Cerro Gordo Cliffs, towards La Herradura, are Cantarriján (nudist/mixed) and El Cañuelo, served by a shuttle bus from 1 June to the end of September, when car access is restricted. Other gems such as Maro beach or Torre del Pino require a short walk down cliff paths; when the sea is calm they offer crystal-clear water and great snorkelling, and dolphins are often seen.

title: Restaurant guide
summary: Personal recommendations from the Zeltmann family after 32 years in Nerja: seafood, meat, tapas, paella, Italian and places with a view.
body: These are personal recommendations, the fruit of many family meals and more than three decades living here. Some are classics and others little discoveries; we hope they help you make the most of your stay.

Seafood and fish. El Mirador de Güilche (Ctra. N-340, boundary between Nerja and Torrox Costa): in our opinion, the best seafood soup in Nerja, rich and made with fresh produce, plus spectacular Mediterranean views. La Pulguilla, La Puntilla and Bar Chispa (old town, near the Balcón de Europa): three classics where fresh fish and tapas rule, with a local feel and good prices. Hostal Avalon (Punta Lara 22): 100 metres from El Playazo, creative international cooking and a large terrace with views of the sea and the mountains (avalonnerja.com).

Meat. Patagonia & Olé (Calle Filipinas, Burriana area): an Argentine grill with a great atmosphere, perfectly cooked steaks, skirt steak and criollo sausages. The Steakhouse at Burriana (Calle Filipinas 1A): good cuts and reasonable prices, perfect after a day at the beach. Paco "El Churretero" (Paseo de Burriana, edificio Tarragona): possibly the best selection of meat in Nerja, with premium cuts (Galician blonde beef, wagyu, ox) over charcoal and an excellent wine list; a little pricier. Café Del Mar y Del Sol (Paseo de Burriana 6): to us, the best beef tenderloin in Nerja, right by the sea.

Tapas and local cooking. Besides La Pulguilla, La Puntilla and Bar Chispa (anchovies, squid, prawns or octopus), there are El Rincón de Pepe (old town, home cooking) and El Sevillano (several spots in the centre, good value and always lively).

Paella and rice. Merendero Moreno (Burriana beach): our favourite paella, made to order and nicely balanced. Ayo (Burriana beach): the most iconic, famous on British TV and for its cooking contests; the "paella of always", cooked outdoors.

Italian and European cuisine. Trattoria Italia (Calle Antonio Ferrandis 29): fresh pasta and wood-fired pizza; open daily 12:30-22:30, Thursdays 17:00-22:30, closed Wednesdays (tel. +34 951 328 180, trattoriaitalianerja.es). L'Antica Nonna Mia (Plaza de los Cangrejos): fresh pasta and traditional dishes made to order (lanticanonnamia.com). Pinocho: run by a Spanish family but with excellent Italian food at reasonable prices. La Dama (Calle Carabeo): perhaps the most affordable Italian option, on one of the most charming streets. Portofino (Calle Puerta del Mar 4): next to the Balcón de Europa, with a terrace over Calahonda beach, artisan pizzas and fresh pasta.

Charm and views. Restaurante Oliva (Plaza de España 2, next to the Balcón): modern Mediterranean cooking with a gourmet touch, recommended by the Michelin Guide, ideal for a special occasion. Número 34 (Calle Carabeo): one of the loveliest, with sea views, several terraces and an indoor pool; a romantic setting. Lamalaka (Calahonda beach, next to the Balcón): modern design and a chill-out terrace with direct access to the sand, open 10:00-00:00 (tel. +34 952 180 824 / 659 341 457, lamalakanerja.com). Bruxelles (Paseo de Playa Burriana): a Belgian-Mediterranean classic famous for its mussels in many styles, plus dishes rarely found in the area such as frogs' legs and snails.

Tips. In high season (June to September) it is worth booking at the most popular places. People dine late in Nerja: locals tend to arrive from 21:00. For groups or families, ask about the set menu or sharing dishes. And above all, take your time: Nerja tastes better when you eat slowly, with a sea view.

title: Breakfast in Nerja
summary: From lifelong local bars a couple of minutes from home to charming cafés or breakfast by the sea.
body: For something quick and simple: Bar La Parada, next to the bus stop on Avenida Pescia, is handy for starting the day with a good coffee and toast, and it is just a minute and a half on foot from Casa Isolde and Casa Florence. Right opposite there is another bar with varied breakfast menus if you fancy a change.
In Plaza Cantarero there are several spots to have breakfast outdoors in a quiet, central square, perfect for watching village life go by.

For more charm: Mena Garden (Calle El Barrio), in the old town, with a lovely interior patio and an international menu (fresh fruit, avocado sandwiches); and Tetería Zaidín (Calle Granada), relaxed with a Moroccan-style patio, ideal for a green tea, home-made pastries or a different breakfast. Cafetería París (near Calle Castilla Pérez) is a classic for good coffee and friendly service.
By the sea: if you prefer breakfast right on the beachfront, Merendero Moreno or Chiringuito José Cruz on Burriana beach are excellent choices.

title: White villages of the Axarquía
summary: Just a few kilometres away: Frigiliana, El Acebuchal, Torrox, Cómpeta, Comares… sea and mountains in under an hour.
body: Frigiliana, just 7 kilometres away (10-15 minutes), is considered one of the most beautiful white villages in Andalusia. Its historic centre, the Moorish quarter of Barribarto, is a maze of narrow whitewashed lanes that evokes its Al-Andalus past. It is known for its history of the Three Cultures (Jewish, Muslim and Christian); the Lizar irrigation channel, of Andalusi origin and possibly more than a thousand years old, is still in use. It is also a gateway to the mountains, with trails up to El Fuerte (Peñón de Frigiliana, almost 1,000 m) and into the Sierra de Almijara.

Very close by, about 30 minutes towards Torrox Pueblo, is El Acebuchal, known to the British as "The Lost Village": a restored hamlet in the mountains reached along an unpaved track passable by an ordinary car, with a wonderful restaurant serving game (fallow deer, venison, wild boar).

A mountain route: from Frigiliana you can carry on to Torrox village (which keeps its traditional white charm, beyond Torrox Costa) and to Cómpeta, another lovely white village known for its sweet moscatel wine and its artistic, international feel.

Back to the coast: from Cómpeta you descend via Sayalonga (famous for its circular cemetery, unique in Spain) and through Algarrobo village and Algarrobo Costa, to join the A-7 back to Nerja: a very pretty circular route between mountains and sea.

Other gems of the Axarquía: Comares, the highest village in the region (about 700 m), of Arab layout and with spectacular views; and Canillas de Aceituno, at the foot of La Maroma (2,069 m, the highest peak in Málaga province), one of the most popular starting points for hiking.

title: Arrival, parking and getting around
summary: How to get here from Málaga, where to park and how to get around Nerja during your stay.
body: By car: Nerja is an hour from Málaga and its airport via the A-7. Our street, Joaquín Herrera, is a quiet residential area where street parking is usually easy; there are also public car parks towards the centre.
By bus: ALSA connects Málaga and the airport with Nerja's bus station directly and frequently.
Nerja is best enjoyed on foot: from the apartment you can walk to the beach, the centre and the Balcón de Europa. For the Maro coves and the white villages, a car is most convenient.

title: Check-out instructions
summary: A short list to leave the apartment ready on your departure day. Check-out is before 10:00 am.
body: On your departure day we ask you to leave the apartment before 10:00 am. These simple steps help us have everything ready for the next guests.
Rubbish: take out all the rubbish, including the bathroom bin, to the street containers.
Fridge: remove any open or perishable food you have left.
Dishes: leave the plates, glasses and cutlery clean and put away in the cupboards.
Electricity: switch off the air conditioning and all the lights, indoors and outdoors.
Closing up: close all doors and windows properly.
Keys: leave one key on the white key rack. Lock the door with the other key and drop it into the mailbox next to it.
Any last-minute questions, message us on WhatsApp at +34 609 549 664. Have a safe trip!

title: Anything at all, just message us
summary: We're just one message away throughout your stay.
body: For anything you need — recommendations, an issue or extending your stay — message us on WhatsApp at +34 609 549 664. We reply in Spanish, English, German, French and Italian.
